coconut shell.sustainability_notes: High calorific value; excellent for activated carbon production used in water purification.
coconut shell.risks: Minimal – ensure dry storage to prevent mold.

rice husk.sustainability_notes: Rice husk ash is a pozzolanic material used in green cement to reduce CO2 emissions.
rice husk.risks: Dust inhalation risk during handling – use masks.

banana peel.sustainability_notes: High potassium content makes banana peel ideal compost additive.

food waste.sustainability_notes: Converting food waste to biogas reduces methane emissions from landfill.
food waste.risks: Pathogen risk if not processed promptly. Store separately.
food waste.compliance_notes: Solid Waste Management Rules 2016 mandate source segregation of bio-degradable waste. Bulk generators (hotels, canteens >100 kg/day) must process on-site or via authorised processor.
food waste.required_handling: Sealed leak-proof containers. Collect daily. Wear gloves. Store away from dry waste.
food waste.knowledge_source: CPCB SWM Rules 2016; MNRE National Biogas and Manure Management Programme; IPCC AR6 methane emission factors
food waste.collection_frequency: Daily — pathogen risk increases rapidly in heat
food waste.preparation_before_sale: Drain excess liquid. Remove non-organic items (plastic bags, cling film). Contact nearest biogas plant — most provide free collection for >50 kg/day.

textile waste.sustainability_notes: Textile recycling saves 1.7 kg CO2 per kg of fiber recovered.
textile waste.risks: Chemical dyes may require pre-treatment before recycling.

plastic bottles.sustainability_notes: Recycling 1 tonne of PET saves 1.5 tonnes of CO2 vs virgin plastic.
plastic bottles.risks: Contamination from residual liquids. Rinse before collection.

glass bottles.composition: Silica 70%, soda ash, lime – recyclable indefinitely
glass bottles.sustainability_notes: Glass is 100% recyclable with no quality degradation.
glass bottles.risks: Handle with care – sharp edges. Use gloves.

cardboard.sustainability_notes: Each tonne of recycled cardboard saves 17 trees and 7000 liters of water.
cardboard.risks: Wet cardboard loses value – store dry.
cardboard.compliance_notes: Solid Waste Management Rules 2016 — classified as dry recyclable waste. Must not be landfilled when recyclable.
cardboard.required_handling: Keep dry. Flatten boxes to reduce volume. Remove tape and staples.
cardboard.knowledge_source: CPCB SWM Guidelines 2016; Fibre Box Association recycling data
cardboard.collection_frequency: Weekly for offices; fortnightly for other facilities
cardboard.preparation_before_sale: Flatten all boxes. Remove plastic tape, foam inserts, and labels. Bundle in stacks of minimum 10 kg. Local kabadiwala collects for ₹4–12/kg depending on volume.

paper waste.composition: Cellulose fiber, wood pulp, bleaching agents
paper waste.sustainability_notes: Recycling 1 tonne of paper saves 1.5 tonnes of CO2 emissions.
paper waste.risks: Confidential documents must be shredded before recycling.

e-waste.composition: Gold, silver, copper, palladium, lead, mercury, cadmium, brominated flame retardants
e-waste.sustainability_notes: E-waste contains 40-50x more gold than gold ore. Proper recycling is critical.
e-waste.risks: CRITICAL: Contains lead, mercury, cadmium – highly toxic. NEVER dispose in regular bins. Causes soil and groundwater contamination. Legal liability under E-Waste Management Rules 2022.
e-waste.compliance_notes: E-Waste Management Rules 2022 (India) — mandatory EPR. Only CPCB/SPCB authorized recyclers may process. Data destruction required under IT Act 2000 Section 43A before handover.
e-waste.required_handling: Do not dismantle, burn, or dump in acid baths. Wipe data before handover. Label as e-waste. Wear gloves.
e-waste.knowledge_source: CPCB E-Waste Management Rules 2022; MoEF Notification GSR 338(E); IT Act 2000
e-waste.collection_frequency: Annually or when decommissioned — do not hoard
e-waste.preparation_before_sale: 1. Data wipe (DoD 5220.22-M standard or physical degauss). 2. List all items with serial numbers. 3. Contact CPCB-certified recycler for collection. Many provide free pick-up for bulk quantities.

aluminium cans.sustainability_notes: Recycling aluminium uses 95% less energy than virgin production.
aluminium cans.risks: Clean and separate from other metals for maximum value.
aluminium cans.compliance_notes: No special regulatory requirement. Export of aluminium scrap requires Customs clearance above threshold quantities.
aluminium cans.required_handling: Compress cans to reduce volume. Keep separate from steel and copper.
aluminium cans.knowledge_source: Aluminium Association of India; World Aluminium LCA Database 2023
aluminium cans.collection_frequency: Weekly for canteens with >20 kg/week; monthly otherwise
aluminium cans.preparation_before_sale: Rinse and crush cans. Bundle or bale. Separate aluminium sheet and extrusions from cans for better pricing.

steel scrap.sustainability_notes: Recycled steel uses 60% less energy than primary steel production.
steel scrap.risks: Sharp edges. Rust may reduce value.

wood waste.sustainability_notes: Wood waste bioenergy can offset fossil fuel use significantly.
wood waste.risks: Treated or painted wood may contain VOCs – separate before processing.

sawdust.sustainability_notes: Sawdust is excellent substrate for oyster mushroom cultivation.
sawdust.risks: Fine dust – inhalation hazard during handling.

construction debris.composition: Concrete rubble, bricks, tiles, sand, metal rebar
construction debris.sustainability_notes: Recycled concrete aggregate reduces quarrying and carbon footprint.
construction debris.risks: May contain asbestos in old buildings – require testing before disposal.

used cooking oil.composition: Triglycerides, free fatty acids, glycerol – post-frying degraded oil
used cooking oil.sustainability_notes: 1 liter of used cooking oil produces ~0.85 liters of biodiesel.
used cooking oil.risks: NEVER pour down drain – clogs pipes and contaminates waterways. Legal violations under EPR rules.

rubber tyres.composition: Natural rubber 30%, synthetic rubber, carbon black, steel wire
rubber tyres.sustainability_notes: Rubberized asphalt roads last 20% longer than conventional asphalt.
rubber tyres.risks: Open burning of tyres is illegal and causes toxic emissions. Use only authorized recyclers.

coffee grounds.composition: Organic compounds, caffeine residue, nitrogen, phosphorus
coffee grounds.sustainability_notes: Coffee grounds improve soil nitrogen and repel garden pests naturally.
coffee grounds.risks: Avoid large quantities in compost as acidity may harm plants.

sugarcane bagasse.sustainability_notes: Bagasse-based paper uses 60% less water than wood-pulp paper.
sugarcane bagasse.risks: Self-heating possible in large wet piles – ensure proper ventilation.

corn husk.sustainability_notes: Corn husk ethanol has 52% lower lifecycle GHG than gasoline.
corn husk.risks: Store dry to prevent mold formation.

eggshells.sustainability_notes: Crushed eggshells raise soil pH and provide slow-release calcium.
eggshells.risks: Dried eggshells only – fresh shells may attract pests.

fish waste.composition: Fish bones, scales, offal – high nitrogen and omega content
fish waste.sustainability_notes: Fish meal is the highest-protein animal feed ingredient available.
fish waste.risks: Odor management critical – rapid decomposition. Biocontainment required.

leather scraps.composition: Collagen protein, chromium tanning agents (hazardous), dyes
leather scraps.sustainability_notes: Chrome-tanned leather scraps require special handling to prevent heavy metal leaching.
leather scraps.risks: HIGH RISK: Chrome VI in tanning waste is carcinogenic. Requires certified treatment facility. Do not compost.

cotton waste.sustainability_notes: Recycled cotton reduces water usage by 99% vs virgin cotton production.

coconut coir.sustainability_notes: Coir peat is a sustainable alternative to peat moss for horticulture.
coconut coir.risks: Salt content in brown coir may inhibit plant growth – wash before use.

wet waste.composition: Kitchen scraps, vegetable peels, fruit waste, cooked food
wet waste.sustainability_notes: Wet waste to biogas can supply 20-30% of campus kitchen energy.
wet waste.risks: Must be segregated at source. Delays cause leachate and methane emissions.

dry leaves.composition: Cellulose, lignin, trace minerals – organic carbon source
dry leaves.sustainability_notes: Leaf mulch retains soil moisture and suppresses weeds naturally.
dry leaves.risks: Avoid burning – contributes to air pollution and is restricted in urban areas.

garden waste.composition: Mixed green/brown plant matter, prunings, grass clippings
garden waste.sustainability_notes: On-site composting of garden waste creates premium horticultural compost.
garden waste.risks: Diseased plant material should not be composted – dispose separately.

battery waste.composition: Lead acid (lead, sulfuric acid), Li-ion (lithium, cobalt, nickel), alkaline (zinc, manganese)
battery waste.sustainability_notes: Li-ion batteries contain cobalt worth ₹2000-4000/kg – high recovery value.
battery waste.risks: CRITICAL: Lead acid batteries contain corrosive sulfuric acid. Li-ion batteries can self-ignite. Lithium causes chemical burns. NEVER dispose in general waste. Covered under Batteries Management Rules 2022.
battery waste.compliance_notes: Batteries Management Rules 2022 — mandatory EPR registration for producers. Consumers must return used batteries through authorized collection points. Unauthorized disposal is a punishable offence.
battery waste.required_handling: Store upright in ventilated, cool, dry area. Acid-resistant gloves for lead acid. Fireproof storage for Li-ion. Label 'Hazardous Battery Waste'.
battery waste.knowledge_source: CPCB Batteries Management Rules 2022; BIS IS 1651 (lead acid batteries); UN 38.3 (Li-ion transport)
battery waste.collection_frequency: When batteries fail or devices are decommissioned — do not store long-term
battery waste.preparation_before_sale: Identify battery chemistry (lead acid, Li-ion, NiMH). Contact OEM take-back scheme or CPCB-certified battery recycler. Most offer collection for >50 units.

medical waste.composition: Sharps, bandages, expired medicines, bodily fluids, pathological waste
buyer_types: CPCB authorized biomedical waste treatment facilities only
medical waste.sustainability_notes: Proper disposal prevents spread of infectious diseases and environmental contamination.
medical waste.risks: CRITICAL BIOHAZARD: Contains pathogens, sharps, toxic chemicals. Governed by Biomedical Waste Management Rules 2016. Mandatory color-coded segregation. Unauthorized disposal is a criminal offence under Environment Protection Act.

copper.sustainability_notes: Recycled copper uses 85% less energy than primary smelting and fully retains properties.
copper.risks: Verify copper purity — mixed alloys reduce value. Store separately from iron to prevent galvanic corrosion.
copper.compliance_notes: No specific regulatory requirement for clean copper scrap. Export requires customs declaration. Mixed scrap with hazardous items may require separate handling.
copper.required_handling: Safety gloves. Segregate by purity grade. Keep away from iron to prevent contamination.
copper.knowledge_source: Copper Development Association India; World Copper Factbook; CPCB Metal Scrap Guidelines
copper.preparation_before_sale: Separate bare bright copper from insulated wire. Purity testing by buyer is standard — clean copper commands highest price.

hdpe.composition: High-Density Polyethylene — rigid thermoplastic, milk jugs, pipes, containers
hdpe.sustainability_notes: HDPE is one of the most recycled plastics — 100% recyclable with minimal quality loss.
hdpe.risks: Contamination from chemicals or food residue reduces recyclability. Clean before collection.

ldpe.composition: Low-Density Polyethylene — flexible plastic, bags, films, wraps
ldpe.sustainability_notes: LDPE film recycling prevents single-use bag pollution and conserves petroleum resources.
ldpe.risks: Contamination from food or liquids makes recycling difficult. Must be clean and dry.

concrete.composition: Cement matrix, aggregate (gravel, sand), steel rebar — demolition rubble
concrete.sustainability_notes: Recycled concrete aggregate reduces quarrying and landfill use — core to green construction.
concrete.risks: Test for asbestos, lead paint, or other contaminants in pre-1990 buildings before processing.

bricks.composition: Fired clay, fly ash, cement — reusable or crushable to aggregate
bricks.sustainability_notes: Reclaimed solid clay bricks can be reused directly, saving manufacturing energy.
bricks.risks: Mortar must be cleaned for full value. Broken or mortar-bonded bricks go to aggregate.

gypsum.composition: Calcium sulfate dihydrate — plasterboard, drywall off-cuts
gypsum.sustainability_notes: Recycled gypsum is used as a cement set-retarder, replacing mined gypsum.
gypsum.risks: Never mix with organic waste — gypsum + organics in landfill produces toxic hydrogen sulfide gas.

chemical waste.composition: Solvents, acids, alkalis, laboratory chemicals, industrial process waste
possible_products: none – must be treated or destroyed by licensed facility
buyer_types: CPCB licensed hazardous waste treatment facilities only
chemical waste.sustainability_notes: Proper treatment prevents groundwater contamination and soil toxicity for decades.
chemical waste.risks: CRITICAL HAZARD: Corrosive, flammable, or toxic. Covered under Hazardous Waste Management Rules 2016. Unauthorized disposal is a criminal offence. Requires manifesting and licensed transport.

diesel sludge.composition: Heavy hydrocarbon residue, tank bottom sludge, water-oil emulsion from fuel storage
diesel sludge.sustainability_notes: Co-processing diesel sludge in cement kilns recovers energy and eliminates hazardous landfill disposal.
diesel sludge.risks: HIGH RISK: Flammable vapors, toxic PAHs. Requires licensed transport and disposal. Covered under Hazardous Waste Management Rules.

oil sludge.composition: Used lubricating oil, engine oil residue, water-hydrocarbon emulsion
oil sludge.sustainability_notes: Re-refining used oil uses 66% less energy than refining crude oil from scratch.
oil sludge.risks: HIGH RISK: Contains PAHs, heavy metals, toxic additives. Never drain into sewers or soil.

printer cartridges.composition: Plastic casing, residual toner/ink (carbon black, pigments), metal components
printer cartridges.sustainability_notes: Refilling one cartridge saves ~2.5 kg of CO2 vs. manufacturing a new one.
printer cartridges.risks: Toner particles are a fine dust inhalation risk. Empty cartridges must not be incinerated.

organic sludge.composition: Wastewater treatment sludge — biomass, nutrients, trace metals, pathogens
organic sludge.sustainability_notes: Treated biosolids used as agricultural fertilizer close the nutrient loop and reduce chemical fertilizer demand.
organic sludge.risks: Contains pathogens and possibly heavy metals — require testing and heat treatment before agricultural use.

used oil.composition: Spent lubricating oil, engine oil — degraded base oil with additive residues
used oil.sustainability_notes: Re-refining used engine oil recovers ~2 liters of base oil per 2.5 liters of used oil collected.
used oil.risks: HIGH RISK: Contains carcinogenic polycyclic aromatics (PAHs) and heavy metals. Never drain into soil or drains.
used oil.compliance_notes: Hazardous Waste Management Rules 2016. Requires licensed transporter and authorised re-refinery.
used oil.required_handling: Store in sealed, labelled drums. No open containers. Licensed transport only.
used oil.knowledge_source: CPCB Hazardous Waste Management Rules 2016; BIS IS 1209
used oil.collection_frequency: Monthly or when drums are full
used oil.preparation_before_sale: Drain water and solids from drum base. Label with volume and date collected.

paper.composition: Cellulose fiber, wood pulp, bleaching agents — general mixed office and printing paper
paper.sustainability_notes: Recycling 1 tonne of paper saves 1.5 tonnes CO2 and 17 trees.
paper.risks: Confidential documents must be shredded before recycling. Wet paper loses most of its value.
paper.compliance_notes: Solid Waste Management Rules 2016 — dry waste must be segregated at source.
paper.required_handling: Keep dry and bundled. Remove plastic sleeves, metal clips, and tape.
paper.knowledge_source: Bureau of Indian Standards; CPCB Solid Waste Management Guidelines 2016
paper.collection_frequency: Weekly in offices; fortnightly in canteens
paper.preparation_before_sale: Bundle loosely with twine. Remove staples. Store in dry area. Local kabadiwala collects minimum 10 kg.

newspaper.composition: Groundwood pulp, newsprint — high lignin content, short fiber
newspaper.sustainability_notes: Newspaper recycling diverts high-volume daily waste from landfill.
newspaper.risks: Ink residue may require de-inking at mill. Keep dry.
newspaper.compliance_notes: Solid Waste Management Rules 2016 — segregate from wet waste.
newspaper.required_handling: Bundle and tie. Keep dry. No need for special PPE.
newspaper.preparation_before_sale: Stack and tie in bundles of minimum 5 kg. Keep away from moisture.

office paper.composition: Virgin or recycled wood pulp — bleached, high-brightness printing and writing paper
office paper.sustainability_notes: High-grade office paper fetches premium rates at recyclers due to long fiber content.
office paper.risks: Shred documents containing personal or financial information before recycling.
office paper.compliance_notes: Data Protection rules apply — shred before recycling. Solid Waste Management Rules 2016.
office paper.required_handling: Shred confidential documents. Remove plastic binding and covers.
office paper.preparation_before_sale: Separate white paper from coloured. Shred confidential items. Bundle minimum 5 kg.

mixed paper.composition: Mixed grades of paper — newspapers, cardboard, office paper, magazines
mixed paper.sustainability_notes: Mixed paper is the most commonly recycled grade. Sorting improves value significantly.
mixed paper.risks: Food-contaminated paper reduces value. Remove food packaging before bundling.
mixed paper.compliance_notes: Solid Waste Management Rules 2016 — dry waste segregation required.
mixed paper.preparation_before_sale: Bundle together. Remove plastic bags and food containers.

pet.composition: Polyethylene Terephthalate (PET) — clear/coloured rigid plastic, water and beverage bottles
pet.sustainability_notes: Recycling 1 tonne PET saves 1.5 tonnes CO2 vs virgin production. 100% recyclable.
pet.risks: Contamination from residual liquid reduces value. Rinse bottles before collection.
pet.compliance_notes: Plastic Waste Management Rules 2016 amended 2022 — EPR obligations apply to producers.
pet.required_handling: Rinse bottles. Crush to reduce volume. Remove caps (HDPE — separate).
pet.knowledge_source: CPCB Plastic Waste Management Rules 2016; NAPCOR Recycling Rate Report
pet.preparation_before_sale: Rinse, crush, and bale if volume allows. Remove labels if possible.

pp.composition: Polypropylene — rigid/flexible plastic used in containers, woven bags, auto parts
pp.sustainability_notes: PP recycling saves approximately 88% of the energy used to produce virgin PP.
pp.risks: Multi-layer laminates containing PP are difficult to separate — lower value. Sort by grade.
pp.compliance_notes: Plastic Waste Management Rules 2016 — single-use PP items banned in India from 2022.
pp.required_handling: Clean and dry before collection. Separate from other plastics.
pp.preparation_before_sale: Clean, sort by colour if possible. Compress to reduce volume.

pvc.composition: Polyvinyl Chloride — pipes, cable insulation, window profiles, packaging film
pvc.sustainability_notes: PVC recycling must use specialist facilities — contains chlorine that releases toxic gases if incinerated.
pvc.risks: NEVER incinerate PVC — releases dioxins and hydrogen chloride. Requires specialist recycler. Inform handler of PVC content.
pvc.compliance_notes: Plastic Waste Management Rules 2016. PVC incineration is prohibited under Hazardous Waste Rules.
pvc.required_handling: Label clearly as PVC. Do not mix with other plastics for incineration-based disposal.
pvc.knowledge_source: CPCB Plastic Waste Management Rules 2016; ECVM PVC Recyclability Guidelines
pvc.preparation_before_sale: Separate from other plastics. Label as PVC for recycler.

mixed plastic.composition: Commingled plastic — multiple resin types unsegregated (HDPE, LDPE, PP, PET, PS, PVC)
mixed plastic.sustainability_notes: Mixed plastics are hard to recycle into high-value products — sorting improves value 3-5x.
mixed plastic.risks: Low value due to mixed resins. Sorting recommended before disposal.
mixed plastic.required_handling: Rinse food residue. Sort into resin types where possible.
mixed plastic.preparation_before_sale: Sort where feasible. Bundle separately from hazardous plastics (PVC).

plastic.composition: Generic plastic waste — resin type unspecified
plastic.sustainability_notes: Identifying the resin type (check the recycling triangle number) can increase value 3-5x.
plastic.risks: Mixed resins reduce recyclability. Identify and sort where possible.
plastic.required_handling: Keep dry. Remove food residue. Sort by resin code if possible.
plastic.preparation_before_sale: Sort by resin type (see recycling number 1-7 on packaging). Clean before collection.

glass.composition: Silica 70%, soda ash, lime — recyclable indefinitely without quality loss
glass.sustainability_notes: Glass is 100% recyclable with no quality degradation. Each tonne recycled saves 1.2 tonnes CO2.
glass.risks: Handle with care — sharp edges. Use gloves. Separate broken from intact glass.
glass.compliance_notes: Solid Waste Management Rules 2016 — inert dry waste; must not go to landfill when recyclable.
glass.required_handling: Wear cut-resistant gloves. Pack in sturdy containers. Separate by colour where possible.
glass.knowledge_source: Glass Packaging Institute; CPCB SWM Guidelines 2016
glass.preparation_before_sale: Separate by colour (clear, green, brown). Remove caps and lids. Rinse residue.

clear glass.composition: Flint/clear glass — highest purity silica, used for food and pharmaceutical bottles
clear glass.sustainability_notes: Clear glass commands the highest recycling price and is easiest to reprocess into new containers.
clear glass.risks: Sharp fragments. Handle with gloves. Keep separate from coloured glass for maximum value.
clear glass.required_handling: Gloves mandatory. Pack in boxes — not loose bags. Label 'clear glass only'.
clear glass.knowledge_source: British Glass Manufacturers Confederation; CPCB Guidelines
clear glass.preparation_before_sale: Rinse. Remove lids and metal caps. Keep separate from coloured glass.

colored glass.composition: Chromium/iron oxide tinted glass — green, brown, blue glass bottles
colored glass.sustainability_notes: Coloured glass saves energy when recycled — mixing colours reduces value.
colored glass.risks: Sharp edges. Mixing colours reduces recyclability and market price.
colored glass.required_handling: Gloves. Pack in rigid containers. Sort green from brown if volume allows.
colored glass.knowledge_source: CPCB SWM Guidelines 2016; Glass Packaging Institute
colored glass.preparation_before_sale: Rinse. Sort by colour for maximum value.

steel.composition: Iron-carbon alloy — structural steel, scrap from fabrication, demolition
steel.sustainability_notes: Recycled steel uses 60% less energy than virgin production and is infinitely recyclable.
steel.risks: Sharp edges. Rust reduces value. Keep dry and separate from non-ferrous metals.
steel.compliance_notes: No special regulatory requirement for clean steel scrap. Hazardous coating (lead paint, asbestos wrap) requires declaration.
steel.required_handling: Safety gloves and boots. Segregate from non-ferrous. Avoid mixing with electronic scrap.
steel.knowledge_source: World Steel Association; CPCB Metal Scrap Guidelines
steel.preparation_before_sale: Remove non-steel attachments. Sort heavy gauge from thin sheet. Weigh before collection.

iron.composition: Cast iron, wrought iron, pig iron — higher carbon content than steel
iron.sustainability_notes: Cast iron recycling saves significant energy vs primary iron making from ore.
iron.risks: Heavy — use mechanical handling. Rust reduces purity and price.
iron.compliance_notes: No special regulatory requirement for clean iron scrap.
iron.required_handling: Heavy lifting equipment required. Gloves and boots.
iron.knowledge_source: CPCB Metal Scrap Guidelines; Bureau of Indian Standards
iron.preparation_before_sale: Separate from steel if possible. Remove grease and oil. Weigh before sale.

brass.composition: Copper-zinc alloy — taps, fittings, electrical terminals, decorative items
brass.sustainability_notes: Brass recycling saves 85% of the energy needed to produce primary copper-zinc alloy.
brass.risks: Verify composition — leadbearing brass (e.g. plumbing) has different value than free-cutting brass.
brass.compliance_notes: No special regulatory requirement for clean brass scrap.
brass.required_handling: Keep separate from iron and aluminium. Do not mix alloy grades.
brass.knowledge_source: Copper Development Association India; CPCB Metal Scrap Guidelines
brass.preparation_before_sale: Separate by alloy type where possible. Remove iron fixtures and fittings.

aluminium.composition: Aluminium alloy — cans, foil, extrusions, die castings — 98% recyclable
aluminium.sustainability_notes: Recycling aluminium uses 95% less energy than virgin production. Infinitely recyclable.
aluminium.risks: Clean and separate from steel for maximum value. Painted or anodised aluminium may be slightly lower value.
aluminium.compliance_notes: No special regulatory requirement. Export of aluminium scrap requires Customs clearance.
aluminium.required_handling: Compress cans to reduce volume. Keep separate from other metals.
aluminium.knowledge_source: Aluminium Association of India; World Aluminium LCA Database
aluminium.collection_frequency: Weekly for canteens; monthly for offices
aluminium.preparation_before_sale: Compress cans. Keep extrusions separate from sheet and castings.

scrap metal.composition: Mixed metal scrap — unspecified alloys, ferrous and non-ferrous mixed
scrap metal.sustainability_notes: Sorting mixed scrap into ferrous and non-ferrous fractions can double value.
scrap metal.risks: Sharp edges. Mixed scrap reduces value — sorting improves recovery significantly.
scrap metal.compliance_notes: Verify for hazardous components (batteries, mercury switches) before sale.
scrap metal.required_handling: Gloves and boots. Use magnet to separate ferrous from non-ferrous.
scrap metal.knowledge_source: CPCB Metal Scrap Guidelines; Indian Metal Scrap Trade Association
scrap metal.preparation_before_sale: Use magnet to sort ferrous from non-ferrous. Remove non-metal attachments.

kitchen waste.composition: Food preparation scraps — vegetable peels, cooked food remnants, tea bags, coffee grounds
kitchen waste.sustainability_notes: Kitchen waste to biogas can supply 20-30% of campus kitchen energy needs.
kitchen waste.risks: Must be segregated. Delays cause leachate and methane emissions. Process within 24 hours.
kitchen waste.compliance_notes: Solid Waste Management Rules 2016 mandate segregation of bio-degradable waste at source.
kitchen waste.required_handling: Sealed containers. Daily collection. No mixing with dry waste.
kitchen waste.knowledge_source: CPCB SWM Rules 2016; MNRE Biogas Programme
kitchen waste.preparation_before_sale: Drain excess water. Remove non-organic items. Contact nearest biogas plant.

organic waste.composition: Mixed organic matter — food waste, garden waste, paper, natural fibers
organic waste.sustainability_notes: Organic waste composting avoids methane generation in landfill — significant GHG benefit.
organic waste.risks: Pathogens if not processed promptly. Segregate immediately.
organic waste.required_handling: Sealed bins. Process within 24 hours. Wear gloves.
organic waste.knowledge_source: CPCB SWM Guidelines 2016; MNRE Biogas Guidelines

vegetable waste.composition: Vegetable peels, trimmings, spoiled produce — high moisture, nitrogen-rich
vegetable waste.sustainability_notes: Excellent C:N ratio for composting when mixed with carbon-rich dry material.
vegetable waste.risks: Rapid decomposition — process within 24 hours. Odor management required.
vegetable waste.preparation_before_sale: Remove stickers and packaging. Drain excess water.

fruit waste.composition: Fruit peels, pulp, cores, seeds — high sugar content, rapid fermentation
fruit waste.sustainability_notes: Citrus peels contain limonene — value-added extraction possible at scale.
fruit waste.risks: Rapid decomposition. High sugar accelerates fermentation and odor.
fruit waste.preparation_before_sale: Remove non-organic packaging. Collect in sealed bin.

leaves.composition: Dry leaf litter — cellulose, lignin, trace minerals, organic carbon source
leaves.sustainability_notes: Leaf mulch retains soil moisture, suppresses weeds, and improves soil structure.
leaves.risks: Avoid burning — air quality violation in urban areas. Disease risk if leaves from infected plants composted.
leaves.compliance_notes: Urban local body bylaws prohibit open burning of leaves in most cities.
leaves.required_handling: No special handling required. Stack in designated compost area.
leaves.knowledge_source: CPCB SWM Rules 2016; Horticulture Department Guidelines
leaves.preparation_before_sale: Collect in biodegradable bags or piles. No plastic bags.

tree branches.composition: Woody prunings, branches, stems — lignocellulosic biomass
tree branches.sustainability_notes: Chipped branches make excellent mulch and can be used in boiler fuel programmes.
tree branches.risks: Sharp cut ends. Large branches require mechanical chipping.
tree branches.compliance_notes: Urban local body rules apply for tree-cutting permissions.
tree branches.required_handling: Gloves and protective clothing when handling cut branches.
tree branches.preparation_before_sale: Chip or shred large branches. Stack in designated area.

grass clippings.composition: Fresh grass cuttings — high nitrogen, moisture 75-85%
grass clippings.sustainability_notes: Grass clippings are an excellent nitrogen source ('green' activator) for compost piles.
grass clippings.risks: High nitrogen causes rapid heating and odor in piles. Mix with carbon-rich material.
grass clippings.required_handling: No special handling. Mix with dry (brown) material to prevent matting.
grass clippings.preparation_before_sale: Mix with dry leaves or cardboard to balance C:N ratio.

cooking oil.composition: Triglycerides, free fatty acids — post-frying degraded vegetable oil
cooking oil.sustainability_notes: 1 liter of used cooking oil produces ~0.85 liters of biodiesel, displacing fossil fuel.
cooking oil.risks: NEVER pour down drain — clogs pipes and contaminates waterways. Legal violations under EPR rules.
cooking oil.compliance_notes: FSSAI Food Safety Standards Act — used cooking oil cannot be reused for cooking. EPR obligations for bulk users.
cooking oil.required_handling: Sealed drums only. Label with date and source. Keep away from heat.
cooking oil.knowledge_source: FSSAI Regulations; CPCB Liquid Waste Guidelines; FAME biodiesel standards
cooking oil.collection_frequency: Weekly for canteens; monthly for offices
cooking oil.preparation_before_sale: Filter solids. Store in sealed containers. Contact biodiesel collector — most provide free collection for >50L.

engine oil.composition: Spent lubricating oil, motor oil — degraded base oil with metal particles
engine oil.sustainability_notes: Re-refining engine oil recovers high-quality base oil using 66% less energy than crude oil refining.
engine oil.risks: Contains carcinogenic PAHs and heavy metals. Never drain into soil or drains — punishable under Environment Protection Act.
engine oil.compliance_notes: Hazardous Waste Management Rules 2016. Requires licensed transporter. Must be sold to re-refinery only.
engine oil.required_handling: Sealed labelled drums. No open containers. Licensed transport only.
engine oil.knowledge_source: CPCB Hazardous Waste Rules 2016; MNRE Used Oil Policy
engine oil.collection_frequency: Monthly or when drums are full
engine oil.preparation_before_sale: Drain water from drum base. Label with volume and date. Contact licensed collector.

textiles.composition: Cotton, polyester, nylon, blended fibers — wearable and industrial
textiles.sustainability_notes: Textile recycling saves 1.7 kg CO2 per kg of fiber recovered. Indian textiles sector generates 5.5M tonnes of waste annually.
textiles.risks: Chemical dyes may require pre-treatment. Synthetic-natural blends harder to recycle than pure fiber.
textiles.compliance_notes: Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) notifications for textiles under development (2024). No mandatory compliance yet.
textiles.required_handling: Sort by fiber type where possible. Keep dry. Remove non-textile components (zips, buttons).
textiles.knowledge_source: Confederation of Indian Textile Industry; Ellen MacArthur Foundation Textile Circularity Report
textiles.preparation_before_sale: Sort into wearable, non-wearable, and industrial. Bundle in jute sacks.

fabric.composition: Woven or knitted fabric — cotton, polyester, silk, wool, synthetic blends
fabric.sustainability_notes: Cut fabric waste from garment factories commands higher recycling rates than post-consumer textiles.
fabric.risks: Dyes and finishes may require pre-treatment before recycling.
fabric.compliance_notes: No current mandatory EPR for fabric waste in India.
fabric.required_handling: Bundle by fiber type. Keep dry. Remove non-fabric attachments.
fabric.knowledge_source: CITI Textile Industry Guidelines; Textile Exchange
fabric.preparation_before_sale: Bundle loosely. Sort cotton from synthetic where identifiable.

leather.composition: Collagen protein, chromium tanning agents, dyes — post-processing leather scraps
leather.sustainability_notes: Chrome-tanned leather scraps require special handling to prevent hexavalent chromium leaching.
leather.risks: HIGH RISK: Chrome VI in tanning waste is carcinogenic. Do not compost. Requires certified treatment facility.
leather.compliance_notes: Hazardous Waste Management Rules 2016 apply to chrome-containing leather waste. Requires licensed disposal.
leather.required_handling: Gloves mandatory. Do not burn. Label as chrome-containing waste.
leather.knowledge_source: CPCB Hazardous Waste Rules 2016; Council for Leather Exports guidelines
leather.preparation_before_sale: Separate chrome-tanned from vegetable-tanned leather. Label clearly for handler.

rubber.composition: Natural rubber 30%, synthetic rubber, carbon black, steel wire
rubber.sustainability_notes: Rubberised asphalt roads last 20% longer than conventional roads and reduce road noise.
rubber.risks: Open burning of rubber is illegal — toxic dioxins. Use only authorised recyclers.
rubber.compliance_notes: Hazardous Waste Management Rules 2016 — waste tyres are scheduled hazardous waste. Registered recyclers only.
rubber.required_handling: Store in covered area — fire risk. Do not expose to heat sources.
rubber.knowledge_source: CPCB Hazardous Waste Management Rules 2016; Tyre Recycler Association of India
rubber.preparation_before_sale: Stack upright in covered area. Separate steel-belted from non-steel tyres.

tyres.composition: Natural and synthetic rubber, carbon black, steel cord, fabric reinforcement
tyres.sustainability_notes: Retreading tyres uses 70% less energy than manufacturing new tyres.
tyres.risks: Open burning releases toxic dioxins and is a criminal offence. CPCB-authorized recyclers only.
tyres.compliance_notes: Hazardous Waste Management Rules 2016. Extended Producer Responsibility under EPCA orders.
tyres.required_handling: Stack upright. Cover from weather. No open fires nearby.
tyres.knowledge_source: CPCB HWM Rules 2016; ATMA (Automotive Tyre Manufacturers Association)
tyres.preparation_before_sale: Assess retreading potential first (highest value use). Contact authorised recycler.

tyre.composition: Natural and synthetic rubber, carbon black, steel cord — worn vehicle tyre
tyre.sustainability_notes: One recycled truck tyre = 6.5 kg of crumb rubber usable in sports surfaces or asphalt.
tyre.risks: Open burning is illegal. Use CPCB-authorized recyclers only.
tyre.required_handling: Store in covered, dry area. Keep away from heat and ignition sources.
tyre.preparation_before_sale: Contact certified recycler. Check retreading eligibility.

wood.composition: Cellulose, lignin, hemicellulose — natural untreated wood
wood.sustainability_notes: Wood waste bioenergy offsets fossil fuel use. Biochar sequesters carbon for decades.
wood.risks: Treated or painted wood may contain VOCs and lead — separate from clean wood before processing.
wood.compliance_notes: No special regulatory requirement for clean untreated wood. Treated wood requires declaration.
wood.required_handling: Separate treated from untreated wood. Keep dry.
wood.knowledge_source: Forest Research Institute; MNRE Biomass Programme
wood.preparation_before_sale: Remove nails and metal fixtures. Chip large pieces if possible.

plywood.composition: Laminated wood veneers bonded with urea/phenol formaldehyde resin
plywood.sustainability_notes: Plywood contains adhesive resins — recovery value is lower than clean wood but still divertible from landfill.
plywood.risks: Formaldehyde in resins — do not burn indoors. Separate from clean wood for processing.
plywood.compliance_notes: No specific regulation for untreated plywood scrap. Burning restricted in urban areas.
plywood.required_handling: Separate from clean solid wood. Keep dry. Do not burn indoors.
plywood.knowledge_source: Forest Research Institute; CPCB SWM Guidelines
plywood.preparation_before_sale: Remove nails and screws. Stack neatly. Label as 'bonded wood' for recycler.

pallets.composition: Solid wood or plywood — pallet boards and stringers
pallets.sustainability_notes: Repairing and reusing pallets is far higher value than chipping — check condition before disposal.
pallets.risks: Pallets treated with methyl bromide (MB marked) are hazardous — do not chip or burn.
pallets.compliance_notes: ISPM 15 (International Plant Protection Convention) — heat-treated pallets (HT mark) are safe for reuse.
pallets.required_handling: Check for MB or HT stamp. Segregate damaged from intact pallets.
pallets.preparation_before_sale: Sort by condition — good (resale), damaged (repair), broken (chip). Stack in batches.

tiles.composition: Ceramic, porcelain, or terracotta clay — fired inert material
tiles.sustainability_notes: Crushed tiles are an excellent sub-base aggregate for road construction and landscaping.
tiles.risks: Sharp fragments during handling. Use gloves and boots.
tiles.compliance_notes: Solid Waste Management Rules 2016 — construction waste must not go to municipal landfill.
tiles.required_handling: Gloves and boots. Contain breakage in covered skips.
tiles.knowledge_source: CPCB Construction Waste Guidelines 2016; Central Building Research Institute
tiles.preparation_before_sale: Break into smaller pieces if needed. Remove grout. Store in skip.

asbestos.composition: Chrysotile or amphibole asbestos fiber — bonded in cement or insulation board
possible_products: none — must be encapsulated and safely landfilled
buyer_types: CPCB licensed hazardous waste disposal facilities only
asbestos.sustainability_notes: No recovery pathway. Safe containment and disposal is the only responsible option.
asbestos.risks: CRITICAL: Asbestos fibers cause mesothelioma and lung cancer. Any disturbance releases carcinogenic fibers. NEVER drill, cut, sand, or break asbestos-containing material. This is a notifiable hazard.
asbestos.compliance_notes: Hazardous Waste Management Rules 2016. Asbestos handling requires licensed contractors. Disposal only at engineered hazardous waste landfill.
asbestos.required_handling: CRITICAL: Full respiratory protection (P3 filter mask), disposable coveralls, gloves. Wet-wrap in double polythene. Do not disturb if intact — encapsulation preferred.
asbestos.knowledge_source: CPCB Hazardous Waste Management Rules 2016; WHO Asbestos Elimination Guidelines
asbestos.preparation_before_sale: Do not attempt to prepare for sale. Contact licensed asbestos removal contractor only.

computers.composition: Desktop computers — PCB, CPU, RAM, HDD, PSU, aluminium/steel chassis, copper wiring
computers.sustainability_notes: A computer PCB contains 40-50x more gold per tonne than gold ore. Responsible recycling is critical.
computers.risks: CRITICAL: Contains lead solder, cadmium, mercury, brominated flame retardants. Toxic to humans and environment. E-Waste Management Rules 2022 mandate authorised recyclers only.
computers.compliance_notes: E-Waste Management Rules 2022 — mandatory EPR obligations. Disposal only through CPCB/SPCB authorized recyclers.
computers.required_handling: Do not dismantle. Wipe data (DoD 5220.22-M standard) before handover. Store in ESD-safe packaging.
computers.knowledge_source: CPCB E-Waste Management Rules 2022; WEEE Directive
computers.preparation_before_sale: Data wipe mandatory. Remove accessories. Contact authorized e-waste vendor.

laptops.composition: Laptop computer — Li-ion battery, LCD screen, PCB, aluminium shell, copper traces
laptops.sustainability_notes: Li-ion battery recycling recovers lithium, cobalt, and nickel — critical for EV manufacturing.
laptops.risks: CRITICAL: Li-ion battery can self-ignite if damaged. Lead, mercury, cadmium in PCB. E-Waste Management Rules 2022.
laptops.compliance_notes: E-Waste Management Rules 2022. Data wiping under IT Act 2000.
laptops.required_handling: Do not puncture battery. Data wipe before handover. Store away from flammables.
laptops.collection_frequency: When decommissioned or at end of lifecycle
laptops.preparation_before_sale: Data wipe (DoD or NIST 800-88). Remove accessories. Package to prevent screen damage.

mobile phones.composition: Smartphone — Li-ion battery, LCD/OLED screen, PCB, camera module, sensors
possible_products: gold, silver, palladium recovery from PCB
mobile phones.sustainability_notes: Mobile phone PCBs contain more gold per kg than gold ore — high intrinsic value when properly recycled.
mobile phones.risks: CRITICAL: Li-ion fire risk if punctured. Lead, cadmium, beryllium in components. E-Waste Management Rules 2022.
mobile phones.compliance_notes: E-Waste Management Rules 2022. Factory reset required for data protection under IT Act.
mobile phones.required_handling: Factory reset and remove SIM/SD card. Do not crush or puncture.
mobile phones.knowledge_source: CPCB E-Waste Management Rules 2022; GSMA Mobile Industry Guidelines
mobile phones.preparation_before_sale: Factory reset. Remove SIM and memory card. Pack safely.

phones.composition: Mobile phones, smartphones, feature phones — Li-ion battery, PCB, display
phones.sustainability_notes: Smartphones contain over 60 elements including critical rare earth metals.
phones.risks: CRITICAL: Li-ion fire risk. E-Waste Management Rules 2022.
phones.required_handling: Factory reset. Do not physically damage. Remove SIM card.
phones.preparation_before_sale: Factory reset. Remove SIM and SD. Pack in original box if available.

monitors.composition: LCD monitor — backlight, LCD panel, PCB, plastic housing, copper wiring
monitors.sustainability_notes: LCD monitors contain indium in the display — a critical rare earth metal recovered through specialist recycling.
monitors.risks: CRITICAL: CRT monitors (older models) contain up to 4 kg of lead — critical hazard. LCD contains fluorescent lamps (mercury) in older models. E-Waste Management Rules 2022.
monitors.compliance_notes: E-Waste Management Rules 2022. CRT monitors are scheduled hazardous waste.
monitors.required_handling: Do not break CRT screens. Handle LCD with care to avoid fluorescent lamp breakage.
monitors.preparation_before_sale: Label CRT vs LCD. Do not dismantle. Contact authorized e-waste recycler.

printers.composition: Inkjet/laser printer — PCB, rollers, motors, toner/ink cartridges, plastic casing
printers.sustainability_notes: Printer cartridges should be removed and recycled separately — they have higher individual recovery value.
printers.risks: Toner powder is a fine carcinogenic dust. Do not dismantle without PPE. E-Waste Management Rules 2022.
printers.required_handling: Remove cartridges separately before disposal. Do not expose to heat.
printers.preparation_before_sale: Remove cartridges. Keep in original box if possible. Contact authorized e-waste recycler.

ups batteries.composition: Valve-regulated lead acid (VRLA) batteries — lead plates, sulfuric acid electrolyte, ABS casing
ups batteries.sustainability_notes: Lead acid batteries have one of the highest recycling rates globally (~95%). Lead is almost infinitely recyclable.
ups batteries.risks: CRITICAL: Corrosive sulfuric acid, heavy lead content. NEVER dispose in general waste. Batteries Management Rules 2022.
ups batteries.compliance_notes: Batteries Management Rules 2022 — mandatory EPR for producers. Disposal only through authorized recyclers.
ups batteries.required_handling: Do not tip or puncture. Wear acid-resistant gloves. Store upright in ventilated area.
ups batteries.collection_frequency: When at end of life (typically 3-5 years)
ups batteries.preparation_before_sale: Contact OEM or authorized battery recycler. Many provide collection service.

lead acid batteries.composition: Lead plates, sulfuric acid electrolyte, polypropylene casing — automotive and industrial
lead acid batteries.sustainability_notes: Lead acid batteries have the highest recycling rate of any product (~99% in India).
lead acid batteries.risks: CRITICAL: Corrosive sulfuric acid. Explosive hydrogen gas if sparks nearby. Lead is highly toxic. Batteries Management Rules 2022.
lead acid batteries.compliance_notes: Batteries Management Rules 2022. Transport as hazardous goods.
lead acid batteries.required_handling: Store upright. Acid-resistant gloves. Ventilated storage. No sparks near storage.
lead acid batteries.knowledge_source: CPCB Batteries Management Rules 2022; BIS IS 1651
lead acid batteries.collection_frequency: When battery fails or is replaced
lead acid batteries.preparation_before_sale: Do not crack or tip. Contact authorized recycler — most offer buy-back for large lead content.

lithium batteries.composition: Lithium-ion or lithium-polymer cells — lithium, cobalt oxide, graphite, electrolyte
lithium batteries.sustainability_notes: Li-ion battery materials (cobalt, lithium) are critical for EV manufacturing — high future value.
lithium batteries.risks: CRITICAL: Thermal runaway risk if punctured, crushed, or overheated — can cause fire. NEVER dispose in regular bins. Batteries Management Rules 2022.
lithium batteries.compliance_notes: Batteries Management Rules 2022. Air transport prohibited for damaged or defective cells.
lithium batteries.required_handling: Do not pierce, crush, or expose to heat. Store in fireproof container if damaged.
lithium batteries.knowledge_source: CPCB Batteries Management Rules 2022; UN 38.3 transport regulations
lithium batteries.preparation_before_sale: Discharge to 30%. Package in fireproof bag. Contact authorized Li-ion recycler.

fluorescent lamps.composition: Glass tube, mercury vapour, phosphor coating, aluminium end caps
fluorescent lamps.sustainability_notes: Mercury from fluorescent lamps is recoverable and reusable — prevents soil and water contamination.
fluorescent lamps.risks: HIGH RISK: Each lamp contains 3-5 mg mercury — causes neurological damage. NEVER break lamps. Do not dispose in general waste.
fluorescent lamps.compliance_notes: Hazardous Waste Management Rules 2016. Mercury is a scheduled hazardous substance under the Minamata Convention (India signatory).
fluorescent lamps.required_handling: Handle intact. Store in original packaging or cardboard tubes. Do not break. Ventilate storage area.
fluorescent lamps.knowledge_source: CPCB HWM Rules 2016; Minamata Convention; UNEP Mercury Guidelines
fluorescent lamps.preparation_before_sale: Keep intact in cardboard sleeve. Bundle in batches. Label as 'mercury-containing lamps'.

led bulbs.composition: LED chips, aluminium heat sink, driver PCB, plastic/glass cover
led bulbs.sustainability_notes: LED bulbs contain no mercury — safer than fluorescent. Aluminium heat sink is high-value.
led bulbs.risks: Low hazard. Driver PCB contains trace lead solder. Do not crush — dispose as e-waste, not general waste.
led bulbs.compliance_notes: E-Waste Management Rules 2022 — lamps with PCBs classified as e-waste.
led bulbs.required_handling: No special PPE required. Keep intact to prevent PCB dust.
led bulbs.knowledge_source: CPCB E-Waste Management Rules 2022; BEE LED Standards
led bulbs.preparation_before_sale: Collect in cardboard box. Contact e-waste recycler.

ink cartridges.composition: Plastic casing, residual ink (organic solvents, pigments), copper contacts
ink cartridges.sustainability_notes: Refilling one ink cartridge saves ~2.5 kg CO2 vs manufacturing a new one.
ink cartridges.risks: Ink pigments may be toxic. Do not incinerate. Residual ink is a mild skin irritant.
ink cartridges.required_handling: Wear gloves when handling — ink can stain and may irritate skin.
ink cartridges.knowledge_source: CPCB E-Waste Management Rules 2022; Printer manufacturers' EPR guidelines
ink cartridges.preparation_before_sale: Cap the cartridge. Collect in sealed plastic bag. Drop at OEM collection point or refiller.

toner.composition: Fine carbon black polymer powder — iron oxide particles, wax, resin binder
toner.sustainability_notes: Toner refilling reduces cartridge manufacturing energy by ~70% per cycle.
toner.risks: Fine toner dust is a carcinogen if inhaled. Do not empty cartridges manually. Do not incinerate.
toner.compliance_notes: E-Waste Management Rules 2022. Toner is classified as fine particulate hazard.
toner.required_handling: Do not open or tap cartridge. Wear gloves. Use in ventilated area only.
toner.knowledge_source: CPCB E-Waste Management Rules 2022; OSHA Toner Dust Safety Guidelines
toner.preparation_before_sale: Seal cartridge opening with tape. Store in original packaging or sealed bag.

tea waste.composition: Spent tea leaves and tea bags — organic matter, nitrogen, tannic acid, some fiber
tea waste.sustainability_notes: Spent tea improves soil drainage and adds nitrogen. Tannic acid acts as natural pest deterrent.
tea waste.risks: Teabags with synthetic mesh (nylon) must be separated from natural fiber bags — nylon does not compost.
tea waste.compliance_notes: Solid Waste Management Rules 2016 — biodegradable waste.
tea waste.required_handling: No special handling. Drain liquid. Remove nylon tea bag mesh.
tea waste.knowledge_source: CPCB SWM Guidelines 2016; TeaCycle UK Composting Standards
tea waste.preparation_before_sale: Drain excess liquid. Mix with coffee grounds or food waste for collection.

ash.composition: Residual mineral matter from wood, coal, or biomass combustion — silica, calcium, potassium
ash.sustainability_notes: Wood ash is a direct substitute for agricultural lime — raises soil pH and provides potassium.
ash.risks: Fine dust inhalation hazard. Coal/industrial ash may contain heavy metals and PAHs — test before agricultural use.
ash.compliance_notes: Fly ash from thermal power plants governed by Fly Ash Notification 2021. Coal ash may require hazardous waste declaration.
ash.required_handling: Dust mask during handling. Wet-suppress to prevent airborne dust. Identify source before disposal.
ash.knowledge_source: MoEF Fly Ash Notification 2021; CPCB Ash Management Guidelines
ash.collection_frequency: After combustion events or daily for continuous kilns
ash.preparation_before_sale: Identify ash type (wood, coal, fly ash). Test pH and heavy metal content before agricultural use.

fly ash.composition: Fine aluminosilicate particles from coal combustion — SiO2 60%, Al2O3 25%, Fe2O3, CaO
fly ash.sustainability_notes: Fly ash as cement replacement reduces CO2 by 0.85 tonnes per tonne of cement replaced.
fly ash.risks: Fine inhalation hazard. May contain trace heavy metals and radioactive elements — use certified testing.
fly ash.compliance_notes: MoEF Fly Ash Notification 2021 mandates 100% utilisation by thermal power plants. Classified as inert waste if tested compliant.
fly ash.required_handling: Dust mask and gloves. Wet suppression during handling.
fly ash.knowledge_source: MoEF Fly Ash Notification 2021; IS 3812 (BIS fly ash standards)
fly ash.collection_frequency: Continuous from power plants; periodic from boilers
fly ash.preparation_before_sale: Test for heavy metals. Contact cement company — most have fly ash procurement programs.

mixed municipal waste.composition: Unsegregated household and commercial waste — organics, paper, plastic, glass, metal, inerts
mixed municipal waste.sustainability_notes: Segregation at source recovers 3-5x more value from the same waste. Mixed waste has the lowest recovery rate of all streams.
mixed municipal waste.risks: Hazardous items (batteries, chemicals) mixed in unsegregated waste create safety risks for handlers.
mixed municipal waste.compliance_notes: Solid Waste Management Rules 2016 mandate source segregation. Generators can be fined for non-compliance.
mixed municipal waste.required_handling: Implement source segregation urgently — wet, dry, and hazardous bins. This is the single highest-impact action.
mixed municipal waste.knowledge_source: CPCB SWM Rules 2016; National Green Tribunal Orders on waste segregation
mixed municipal waste.preparation_before_sale: Do not sell — implement source segregation first. Contact municipal agency for dry and wet bins.

hazardous waste.composition: Generic hazardous waste — specific composition unknown; may include chemicals, oils, solvents, heavy metals
possible_products: none until classified — refer to specific material entry
buyer_types: CPCB licensed hazardous waste treatment facilities only
hazardous waste.sustainability_notes: Proper classification and disposal prevents groundwater contamination and soil toxicity for decades.
hazardous waste.risks: CRITICAL: Do not handle, move, or dispose of unclassified hazardous waste without professional assessment. Legal liability under Environment Protection Act 1986.
hazardous waste.compliance_notes: Hazardous Waste Management Rules 2016. Unauthorized disposal is a criminal offence under EPA 1986.
hazardous waste.required_handling: CRITICAL: Do not touch without PPE. Isolate from other waste. Call licensed hazardous waste contractor.
hazardous waste.knowledge_source: CPCB Hazardous Waste Management Rules 2016; EPA 1986
hazardous waste.preparation_before_sale: Classify using CPCB Schedule I/II/III. Contact licensed treatment facility.
